newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Korean shares surge on hot local market.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Korean shares surge on hot local market.

text.p: Korean global depositary receipts surged on Wednesday, rising by seven percent to outpace a hot Seoul market, traders said.
"Much of the gain was following up on New York," a trader said, "Semi-conductor stocks are strong and we are seeing few natural sellers."
The benchmark three-year corporate yields hit a three-month low of 11.98 percent, driving the Seoul composite index gained 14.77 points, or 2.04 percent, to 738.12.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index gained 4.74 points to 72.49 points, a premium of 46.59 percent over the local market.
"Premiums are very high and there is little to indicate that they are going anywhere but north," a trader said, adding that market makers have been holding inventory.
Chipmaker Samsung Electronics benefited rising $1.60 to $57.10.
The Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.87 points down at 81.29, with the premium over the local market at 26.78 percent from 27.63 percent.
The loss tracked the local market where Bombay's benchmark index closed down 7.25 point to 3685.31.
TELCO finished down 82 cents at $12.50/$13.25 and Indian Hotels gained $1.00 at $22.50/$23.25.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index rose 0.18 points, or 0.16 percent, to 114.83, representing a discount to the local market of 2.55 percent.
